'''John Dirk Walecka''', often quoted as ''J. Dirk Walecka'' (born March 11, 1932) is an American [[theoretical physics|theoretical]] [[nuclear physics|nuclear]] and [[particle physics|particle]] physicist. He is a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]<ref name=apsBonnerRecipient /> and the author of numerous textbooks in physics. Walecka is currently the Governor's Distinguished CEBAF Professor of Physics, emeritus at the [[College of William and Mary]].<ref name=williamMaryDir>{{Cite web|title=Directory - J. Dirk Walecka|url=https://www.wm.edu/as/physics/people/emeritusfaculty/walecka_j.php|access-date=2020-09-13|website=William & Mary|language=en}}</ref>

==Life==
Walecka studied at [[Harvard University]] as an undergraduate, reviving a Bachelor of Arts in 1954,<ref name=williamMaryDir /> and received his doctorate in 1958 under [[Victor Weisskopf]] at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=John Dirk Walecka|url=https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=178964|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=13 September 2020|website=Mathematics Genealogy Project}}</ref> Walecka moved to [[Stanford University]] in 1959, where he was made assistant professor in 1960, upon completing his NSF fellowship, and Professor in 1966. From 1977 to 1982 he was head of the physics faculty and from 1987 he holds the title of emeritus Professor of Physics.<ref name=AIPbio /> From 1986 to 1992 he was the scientific director of the Continuous Electron Beam Accelerator Facility (CEBAF) in [[Newport News, Virginia]].<ref name=AIPbio /> From 1992 he was the Distinguished CEBAF Professor of Physics at the [[College of William and Mary]], where he headed the Nuclear Physics Institute and the Physics Faculty. In 1991 he served as the Distinguished Ship Lecturer at Stanford. Also from 1992 he worked at the [[Thomas Jefferson National Accelerator Facility]].<ref name=AIPbio />

Walecka is the author of a standard work on quantum mechanical many-body theory with Alexander Fetter and a book on many-body methods in theoretical nuclear physics. He was particularly concerned with electron scattering on nuclei. In 2000 he edited [[Felix Bloch]]'s lectures on statistical mechanics (World Scientific).

==Awards==
Walecka has been a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] since 1971.<ref name=apsBonnerRecipient>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=1996 Tom W. Bonner Prize in Nuclear Physics Recipient|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Walecka&first_nm=John&year=1996|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=13 September 2020|website=American Physical Society}}</ref> and was a fellow of the [[National Science Foundation]] from 1958 through 1960, while at [[CERN]] and then [[Stanford]].<ref name=AIPbio>{{Cite web|title=Walecka, John Dirk, 1932-|url=https://history.aip.org/phn/11610034.html|access-date=2020-09-13|website=history.aip.org}}</ref>

In 1996 Walecka received the [[Tom W. Bonner Prize in Nuclear Physics]]. for "his preeminent theoretical guidance and inspirational leadership in exploiting electromagnetic and weak probes of the nucleus and for his fundamental contributions to the understanding of the nucleus as a relativistic quantum many-body system."<ref name=apsBonnerRecipient /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Tom W. Bonner Prize in Nuclear Physics|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/bonner.cfm|access-date=2020-09-13|website=www.aps.org|language=en}}</ref>

In 2009 he received the [[Eugene Feenberg Memorial Medal]] "for theoretical contributions in electroweak interactions with nuclei, the development of relativistic field theories of the nuclear many-body problem and unparalleled achievements in the education of a generation of young nuclear many-body physicists".<ref>{{Cite web|title=Recent Progress in Many Body Theories:Main Page - Recent Progress in Many Body Theories|url=https://rpmbt.physics.indiana.edu/wiki/index.php?title=Recent_Progress_in_Many_Body_Theories:Main_Page#Feenberg_Memorial_Medal|access-date=2020-09-13|website=rpmbt.physics.indiana.edu|language=en}}</ref>

==Publications==
* ''Theoretical nuclear and subnuclear physics'', Oxford University Press 1996
* with [[Alexander L. Fetter]]: ''Quantum theory of many particle systems'', McGraw Hill 1971, Dover 2006
* with Fetter: ''Theoretical mechanics of particles and continua'', McGraw Hill 1980, Dover 2003
* with Fetter: ''Nonlinear Mechanics'', Dover 2006
* ''Introduction to General Relativity'', World Scientific 2007
* ''Introduction to Modern Physics - Theoretical Foundations'', World Scientific 2008
* ''[https://doi.org/10.1017/9781009290616 Electron Scattering for Nuclear and Nucleon Structure]'', Cambridge University Press 2001
* {{cite journal|doi=10.1146/annurev.ns.25.120175.001553|doi-access=free|title=Electron Scattering and Nuclear Structure|year=1975|last1=Donnelly|first1=T. W.|last2=Walecka|first2=J. D.|journal=[[Annual Review of Nuclear Science]]|volume=25|pages=329–405|bibcode=1975ARNPS..25..329D}}
* ''Advanced Modern Physics'', World Scientific Publishing, 2010
* ''Topics in Modern Physics: Theoretical Foundations'', World Scientific Publishing, 2013
* ''Introduction to Electricity and Magnetism'', World Scientific Publishing, 2018
*''Introduction to Classical Mechanics'', World Scientific Publishing, 2020
*''Introduction to Quantum Mechanics'', World Scientific Publishing, 2021
